summary: Clark County tower site also called the Kokaly Lookout Tower; listed as standing, but sources conflict on name and county and give no build or staffing history.

evidence.supports: Association lists the Kokaly tower as standing in Clark County
County list places North Mound (Kokaly) in Clark County as standing
County list gives the same coordinates for North Mound (Kokaly)
TopoZone approximate elevation of 1,401 feet (427 metres)
Older list has a Kokaly entry in Clark County
Older list also has a North Mound entry under Eau Claire County
In 2015 the 72 towers still in use across Wisconsin were decommissioned
evidence.quote: In 2015, the 72 aging towers still in use were decommissioned.

evidence.supports: OpenStreetMap coordinates match the Clark County site

sources.title: Connecting the dots: the fire towers of Wisconsin

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The Forest Lookouts list has a North Mound entry under Eau Claire County, while the Association's county list and TopoZone place the Kokaly tower in Clark County, and OpenStreetMap gives the same coordinates. The record keeps Clark County. The Eau Claire entry is not tied to this site.

notes_for_editor: Only location, elevation and standing status are sourced for this tower. No build date, builder, design, staffing or access appears in any page reached. A Leader-Telegram article on the 2015 closures, which quotes a long-time North Mound staffer, returned HTTP 429 on every attempt and was not read; it is the best lead for this tower's history and worth a retry. The name 'North Mound' versus 'Kokaly' and the Eau Claire County entry need a check against a Wisconsin DNR or Clark County source. Story is short because the evidence is thin.
